fatal_errors: The proposed powder-preheating intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated low-temperature ID-HVAF i7 process and optimized medium air/fuel-pressure setting.
The hypothesis confuses the 15–45 μm feedstock particle-size range with the thickness of the baseline deposit.
The cited evidence concerns a different AlBeSiTiV alloy and does not test powder preheating, FeCoNiCrAl deposition efficiency, or oxidation-resistant bond coats.
No relevant service window is specified or tested, particularly the demonstrated 1000–1150 °C, 50 h isothermal oxidation conditions.
The claim that 200–300 °C powder preheating will materially improve in-flight plasticity and deposition while preserving oxidation is unsupported.
explanation: The response recognizes the desired objectives—greater coating buildup, retained integrity, and low as-sprayed oxidation—and proposes a controlled comparison with an explicit falsification rule. However, it misses the target intervention: optimized low-temperature ID-HVAF deposition produced an approximately 150 μm coating with 79% deposition efficiency and 0.2% porosity. It also omits the relevant torch configuration, substrate preheat, Inconel 718 substrate, BCC phase retention, alumina-TGO mechanism, and high-temperature service boundaries. Its mechanism is only generically plausible and is not supported by the cited paper. The experiment can test the proposed alternative, but it does not establish performance under bond-coat service exposure or assess the decisive alumina-scale behavior.
